text: dsh-tsm-agent（DSH 插件，Web 与 headless 客户端）：接入 DLR 语义问答并显示 TSM 状态。它通过 MCP 连接本机 TSM Core Service，配置语义助手和范式技能；Web 面板显示服务状态、图与向量统计并提供图谱入口。适合需要业务语义建模问答和后端状态查看的 DSH 用户。需要 DeepSeek API 凭据及独立运行的 TSM Core Service。

dsh-tsm-agent adds DLR semantic Q&A to DSH through a local TSM Core Service over MCP. It configures a semantic assistant and paradigm skill; its Web panel shows service status, graph and vector counts, and graph links. Requires a DeepSeek API credential and running TSM service.
想让 DSH 通过本机语义服务回答业务建模问题。
希望在 DSH Web 里看到 TSM 后端是否在线和图谱规模。
I want DSH to answer business modeling questions using my local semantic service.
dsh-tsm-agent 的功能「语义服务接入」：连接本机 TSM Core Service 的 MCP 接口，并配置语义助手 persona 与范式技能，供 DSH 会话调用语义问答工具。
dsh-tsm-agent 的功能「TSM 状态浮层」：Web 客户端定时查询本机多个 TSM 状态端点，显示活跃场景、图后端和节点关系、向量表计数，并提供图谱页面入口。
dsh-tsm-agent 使用前须知：MCP 配置默认连到本机 127.0.0.1:28795，语义请求会发送给该 TSM Core Service；另需配置 DeepSeek API 凭据供模型路由使用。

text: dsh-tsm-agent README · DLR Proj — Decoupled Logic Representation + Three-Level Semantic Modeling：**DLR (Decoupled Logic Representation)** is an original **data-source-level** semantic modeling paradigm: a two-layer model (**LE** logical entities / **PE** physical views) plus two mechanisms (**ARCS** projection anchoring, **PAS** semantic routing). It decouples the logical concept layer from the physical data layer so an LLM agent can land natural-language questions on relational databases reliably. See [docs/03-design.md](docs/03-design.md).
section: DLR Proj — Decoupled Logic Representation + Three-Level Semantic Modeling

text: dsh-tsm-agent README · DLR Proj — Decoupled Logic Representation + Three-Level Semantic Modeling：The project runs DLR inside the **Three-Level Semantic Modeling (TSM)** framework — **L1 `dlr`** (data-source level) / **L2 `consensus`** (domain-consensus level) / **L3 `sop`** (business-logic level). The admission criteria for a piece of knowledge are the governance line. See [docs/02-concept.md](docs/02-concept.md).

dsh-tsm-agent README · Benchmarks：Three external benchmarks, all run end-to-end under this architecture (every case auditable in the ledgers):

**BIRD mini-dev — NL2SQL · 11 databases · 500 questions** · scenario [`birdminidev`](scenarios/birdminidev/)

*EX on BIRD mini-dev (500 q): representative training-free methods on GPT-4o, as reported in the PV-SQL paper (arXiv:2604.17653). Ours: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + TSM+DLR — 426/500 exactly matching gold + 74/500 carried by L3 defect rulings.*

dsh-tsm-agent README · Benchmarks：| Run | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| All 500 questions | **500/500 judged correct** — ✅ 426 matching gold exactly + 🔁 74 ruled correct under L3 clauses (the dataset's own gold is defective on those) | zero errors · median ≈ 56k tokens / ~6 steps per question |

**Cloud-OpsBench — Kubernetes root-cause analysis · 754 cases** (Online Boutique + Train-Ticket) · scenario [`cloudopsbench`](scenarios/cloudopsbench/)

dsh-tsm-agent README · Benchmarks：*Cloud-OpsBench (754 cases): JRA — faulty component + fault type both correct (bars); ECR — evidence chains fully closed (line). Baselines: the benchmark report (arXiv:2603.00468), per-model scores weighted over Online Boutique (550) + Train-Ticket (204). Ours: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + TSM+DLR — JRA 753/754 (99.87%), chains fully closed 740/754 (98.1%), scored by the same upstream scorer.*

dsh-tsm-agent README · Benchmarks：*Six-metric comparison: on every metric, ours sits above the best of the benchmark's 10 published bare models — CA +17.0, FA +24.6, JRA +27.4, MC +28.8, EOC +32.1, ECR +59.9 percentage points (the strongest baseline for each metric is named on its bar). The matrix below is the full field, model by model. Baselines: the benchmark report's per-system tables, weighted over Online Boutique (550) + Train-Ticket (204); ours: the full 754-case run. Baselines are bare models without TSM/DLR and the base model differs (V4-Flash vs V4.1-Flash), so this is a magnitude reference, not a same-model ablation.*

dsh-tsm-agent README · Benchmarks：| Run | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| All 754 cases (100%) | **JRA 753/754 (99.87%)** ✅ · evidence chains fully closed: 740/754 (98.1%) · all six metrics full: 722/754 (95.8%) | process means MC 0.996 / EOC 0.980 · invalid actions 0.8% |
| Reference — model baselines (the benchmark's own scorer) | best published bare model per metric: CA 0.829 · FA 0.754 · JRA 0.725 · MC 0.708 · EOC 0.659 · ECR 0.382, weighted over all 754 (best JRA: DeepSeek-V4-Flash; best ECR: Qwen3-14B) | scored by the upstream scorer as-is; no manual rulings |

Baselines: the benchmark report (arXiv:2610.20424), 3-round means of bare models; ours: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + TSM+DLR — best valid run per case (assisted: DLR tools replace the dataset's knowledge tools; the simulator, record/action tools and verifier are unchanged). 44/50 strict (88%), G/P/F 44/48/49, IF 4%. dsh-tsm-agent README · 1. Start the semantic backend：```bash
bash "DSH-based Agent Service/scripts/start_backend.sh"     # Neo4j + TS MCP server (:28795); idempotent
cd "TSM Core Service" && npx tsx src/verify/precheck.ts     # sanity check — should list 7 tools
```

dsh-tsm-agent README · 2. Ask one question (headless)：```bash
bash "DSH-based Agent Service/dsh_dlr/run_one.sh" 1471 \
  "What is the ratio of customers who pay in EUR against customers who pay in CZK?"
```

The launcher prechecks the backend, runs `dsh --profile headless --json`, and writes the event stream to `tmp_scripts/dsh_smoke/` (or a directory you pass as the third argument).

dsh-tsm-agent README · Architecture：``` dsh (DeepSeek Harness: headless / web) │ MCP (streamable-http :28795, 7 tools) ▼ TSM Core Service (TypeScript): LanceDB (vectors) + ONNX encoder (in-process) Processes: the TS MCP server always; Neo4j only when the `neo4j` graph backend is in use (the default in this repo's `.env`). LanceDB and the encoder are embedded, not services.

dsh-tsm-agent README · Scenario packages：A **scenario** is one complete TSM: content lives in `scenarios/<name>/` and is consumed by the service.

| Layer | Carrier | Tool surface |
|---|---|---|
| L1 `dlr` | `sources/configs/DLR/*.yaml` → graph + vectors | `dlr_semantic_query` → `get_pe_mapping` / `get_le_attrs` |
| L2 `consensus` | `sources/consensus/*.jsonl` → vectors | `dlr_search_consensus` |
| L3 `sop` | `sources/sop.md` → retrieval index (built by `tsm build`) | `dlr_search_sop(question)` |

dsh-tsm-agent README · Scenario packages：Also in the package: `eval/questions.jsonl` (the exam paper — one line per question: `{question, expected, source}`; answer keys come from the L3 clause for the 74 defect-ruled questions, gold otherwise), `results/<run>/` (graded runs), `fixtures/` (truth sets for the verify suite), `DETAIL.md` + `DETAIL/<db>.md` (ledger).

dsh-tsm-agent README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| A question burns its whole timeout with no tool calls | Backend not up: run `start_backend.sh` (the launcher prechecks and stops early) |
| Web UI fails with `EADDRINUSE 3080` | Stale instance: `netstat -ano \| grep :3080` → `taskkill //F //PID <pid>` |
| Tool names unknown to the model after a dsh upgrade | re-check patch rows with `--dump-config` (the bundle is verified on `0.2.0-rc.2`) |
| `tsm grade` appears stuck | Pathological agent SQL is bounded by a 20 s subprocess timeout; slow gold queries are disk-cached (`TSM_GOLD_NO_CACHE=1` bypasses) |
| More rows | [docs/run.md](docs/run.md) troubleshooting table |
